intents.directive: an explicit instruction to use the strongest model, Fable, maximum thinking or the best intelligence for this task ("use best intelligence", "use fable", "max effort", "réfléchis à fond")
intents.trivial: chit-chat, an acknowledgement, a test ping, a progress check ("t'en es où ?") or one given command to run ("lance pnpm dev"); not a go-ahead for pending work, no question about models or routing
intents.resume: a bare go-ahead to continue or start the work already discussed ("reprends", "go", "vas-y", "continue", "do all fixes", "done"), with no new content of its own
intents.git: committing, pushing, rebasing or merging finished work, opening, updating or merging pull requests, splitting atomic commits, resolving a merge or rebase conflict, deleting stale branches or worktrees
intents.explain: a question answered by reading product code, docs, logs or the conversation: why it behaves so, how it works, where it lives, what was done, a diagram; nothing to change yet
intents.plan: planning before any code: how to structure a system, which approach and its trade-offs, research to pick a tool, a multi-step plan, roadmap or spec; not how things work today, not writing code
intents.prod: a production deploy, migration, rollback or live incident to watch closely through logs, errors and metrics, ready to roll back; a mistake reaches real users or data
intents.debug: finding why something is broken when the cause is unknown: a pasted error or failing command, a crash, wrong output or regression to investigate before any fix ("pourquoi ça fail", "check why")
intents.tooling: improving, fixing or asking about the agent's own tooling: pi extensions, skills, AGENTS.md, prompts, model routing, quotas, guards on what agents may run, MCP servers, dotfiles; not product code
intents.frontend: frontend or UI code, design, styling or pixel parity, or reviewing, auditing or simplifying existing code where polish matters; not backend code, not a one-line edit
intents.backend: writing or fixing backend code, APIs, databases, data cleanup, scripts, CI or infra config, or a broad multi-file refactor; not the agent's own tooling, not just running a command
intents.ci: running a build, tests or CI and watching it until it passes, fixing failures and rerunning; local or pull-request work, nothing deployed
intents.staging: deploying to staging or preview, or publishing a package release, then watching logs and health checks until it works; not production
